Whether used on its own or as part of a fantasy asset pack, this Amanita mushroom is a must-have for adding color, playfulness, and natural magic to your digital forest world.

description_text:
Eilean Donan (Scottish Gaelic: Eilean Donnain) is a small tidal island where three sea lochs meet, Loch Duich, Loch Long and Loch Alsh, in the western Highlands of Scotland. A picturesque castle that frequently appears in photographs, film and television dominates the island, which lies about 1 kilometre (5⁄8 mi) from the village of Dornie. Since the castle’s restoration in the early 20th century, a footbridge has connected the island to the mainland.
Eilean Donan is part of the Kintail National Scenic Area, one of 40 in Scotland.[2] In 2001, the island had a recorded population of just one person,[3] but there were no “usual residents” at the time of the 2011 census.[1]
The castle was founded in the thirteenth century, and became a stronghold of the Clan Mackenzie and their allies the Clan MacRae. In the early eighteenth century, the Mackenzies’ involvement in the Jacobite rebellions led in 1719 to the castle’s destruction by government ships (Wikipedia)

The Old Abandoned Rusty Cars pack is a high-detail post-apocalyptic vehicle collection designed for cinematic environments, games, and photorealistic renders. This set captures the visual narrative of long-term abandonment, natural overgrowth, and structural decay.
Design & Style
The overall design follows a post-apocalyptic, urban decay aesthetic, blending mechanical deterioration with organic invasion. The vehicles appear untouched for decades, overtaken by nature and environmental exposure. The style emphasizes realism, surface storytelling, and environmental integration, making it ideal for survival scenes, ruined cities, forest takeovers, and dystopian landscapes.
The forms remain faithful to realistic automotive proportions:

  - The compact car features a rounded, collapsed silhouette with dented panels and corroded surfaces.

  - The cargo van maintains a boxy industrial shape, partially intact but heavily rust-stained and overgrown.

  - The motorcycle frame is skeletal and stripped down, exposing structural geometry.

  - The detached seat and engine block add modular storytelling elements for scene dressing.

Materials

  - All assets are built with physically based rendering (PBR) materials, focusing on layered surface degradation:

  - Oxidized steel with advanced rust variation (dark brown, orange corrosion, flaking metal)

  - Peeling automotive paint with edge wear and exposed primer

  - Dirty glass with grime and opacity variation

  - Rubber components with desaturation and aging

  - Organic foliage materials with leaf translucency and natural color variation

  - Soil and dust accumulation in crevices and lower body sections

Vegetation is integrated directly into the vehicles, with vines wrapping around mirrors, windows, grilles, and interiors. Leaves penetrate broken glass areas and open cavities, reinforcing the sense of time and abandonment.
Colors
The pack features a natural, earthy palette:

  - Deep rust browns

The image is a comprehensive, bright, and creatives stylized low-poly 3D render, bringing together all the distinct building and tree models from the previous individual images into a single, cohesive urban landscape. The scene is set on a much larger, continuous green grassy field with an interconnected network of grey asphalt roads and sidewalks that link the structures and create a functional-looking city block. The specific pedestrian crosswalk is visible on one of the main streets.
Two main multi-story buildings serve as architectural anchors:
On the left, the tall, distinct white building with horizontal brown stripes and large windows is positioned near a junction, as seen in image_9.png.
On the right, the complex, multi-colored (turquoise, orange, blue glass panels) modern residential or office tower is featured, showcasing the detail from image_10.png and image_11.png.

Prominently featured in the light blue sky above the entire scene are two stylized 3D low-poly text elements:
The main title is Low Poly Urban Environment in large, faceted, multi-colored letters.
Below it, a smaller text reads Free Download in orange, faceted letters.
The lighting is bright and warm, casting distinct geometric shadows and highlighting the faceted textures of all objects. Small, added low-poly details like benches, a bus stop sign, and a small park area with a low-poly fountain are included to enhance the creative feel. The entire scene has a playful, miniature world atmosphere.

description_text:
Dianthus gratianopolitanus Grass 01
Dianthus gratianopolitanus, commonly known as the Cheddar pink or clove pink, is a species of plant in the family Caryophyllaceae. It is a herbaceous perennial, hardy to zones 4–8. It grows to a height of 0.5 to 1 feet, blooming from May to June. Flowers are fragrant and rose pink. Grows best in full sun and has medium water requirements. Overwatering or poor drainage leads to crown rot, and plants do not tolerate wet winter soil conditions. The specific epithet gratianopolitanus refers to the ancient Roman name Gratianopolis of the modern French city of Grenoble. The common name Cheddar pink refers to the fact that it's native to the Cheddar Gorge in England. It is native to western and central Europe, from the UK to Ukraine. It became a protected species in the UK in 1975 under the Conservation of Wild Creatures and Wild Plants Act.

  - 2x Albedo/Diffuse (4K)

  - File names (textures & meshes) are simple to understand;

  - Easy modification;

  - Low-mid polycount;

  - Royalty-free licence and free price.

If you have any questions/suggestions, please, write that in a comment section or contact me on my e-mail: andriyandriy1956@outlook.com
Thank you!

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia:The Utah teapot, or the Newell teapot, is a 3D test model that has become a standard reference object and an in-joke within the computer graphics community. It is a mathematical model of an ordinary Melitta-brand teapot that appears solid with a nearly rotationally symmetrical body. Using a teapot model is considered the 3D equivalent of a Hello, World! program, a way to create an easy 3D scene with a somewhat complex model acting as the basic geometry for a scene with a light setup. Some programming libraries, such as the OpenGL Utility Toolkit, even have functions dedicated to drawing teapots.
The teapot model was created in 1975 by early computer graphics researcher Martin Newell, a member of the pioneering graphics program at the University of Utah. It was one of the first to be modeled (using bézier curves) rather than precisely measured.
